_note: INDICATIVE DEFAULTS, MEANT TO BE EDITED. Every threshold in this file is a starting reference, not a fact. Benchmark levels move with market, cycle, accounting regime, interest rates and period. Where you have a real peer set with comparable accounting and aligned fiscal periods, PERCENTILE COMPARISON AGAINST THAT PEER SET OVERRIDES THESE ABSOLUTE BANDS — pass peer_values or peer_percentile in the input and score.py will use it in preference to the band below. Where a company has a long, stable, comparable own history, own-history scoring (basis: own_history) overrides the band too. Treat an unedited run as a first draft of a scorecard, and say so in the report.

_scale.note: Metric values are mapped onto 0-10 by piecewise-linear interpolation between the four threshold anchors. Values beyond the 'excellent' anchor clamp at 10. Values beyond 'poor' fall linearly to 0 over one further band width. 'band' metrics score 10 inside the excellent interval and taper outward. 'judgement' metrics are supplied directly on the 0-10 scale by the analyst, with a written justification.

business_quality.label: Business quality & moat
business_quality.why: Whether the economics are structurally defensible. Everything else decays toward the industry mean without this.

profitability.label: Profitability & returns on capital
profitability.why: What the business earns on the money tied up in it. Return on capital, not margin, is what compounds.

earnings_quality.label: Earnings quality & cash conversion
earnings_quality.why: Whether reported profit turns into cash. Profit is an opinion; cash is a fact.

balance_sheet.label: Balance sheet & solvency
balance_sheet.why: Whether the company survives a bad two years. Solvency is the precondition for every other virtue mattering.

growth.label: Growth & reinvestment
growth.why: Whether there is somewhere to put the next rupee at the same return. Growth without incremental returns destroys value.

governance.label: Governance & management
governance.why: Who controls the cash flows and whether minority owners get their share of them.

valuation.label: Valuation & margin of safety
valuation.why: What the price already assumes. A great business at a price that assumes perfection is a poor investment.

risk.label: Risk
risk.why: Concentration, regulation, cyclicality, key-person and tail exposures that can invalidate the thesis regardless of the fundamentals.

default.note: Balanced quality-and-price view. Use unless the user states an objective.

quality_compounder.note: Long-hold quality bias: pays up for durability, tolerates a fuller price.

deep_value.note: Price and balance-sheet led. Survival and discount matter more than moat.

income.note: Distribution durability led. Cash conversion and solvency dominate.

forensic.note: Fraud-screen bias for a company you already distrust. Use with the gates, not instead of them.

_coverage.note: Composite is emitted as INDICATIVE ONLY when the weight of categories carrying at least one scored metric falls below min_category_coverage, or when any category weighted 10% or more is entirely empty. Missing categories are dropped and the remaining category weights renormalised to 1.0 — never scored as zero. A missing number is not a bad number.

_gates.label: Auditor material uncertainty related to going concern
_gates.why: The auditor is saying the entity may not survive the next twelve months. No margin, return or multiple is meaningful against that. Averaging it into a composite converts a binary survival question into a rounding error.
_gates.evidence_needed: Auditor's report — Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern paragraph; 10-K Item 7 / Note 1 substantial-doubt disclosure.

_gates.label: Active fraud, forensic audit or securities-regulator enforcement on the accounts
_gates.why: If the accounts themselves are under investigation, every input to the scorecard is of unknown reliability. You cannot score numbers you do not believe.
_gates.evidence_needed: SEBI/SFIO/ED order or SEC enforcement action; exchange disclosure of a forensic audit; lender-mandated forensic audit.

_gates.label: Adverse audit opinion or disclaimer of opinion
_gates.why: The auditor has declined to certify the financials. The scorecard has no valid inputs.

_gates.label: Debt default, rating at D, or covenant breach not waived
_gates.why: Equity in a defaulting capital structure is an option, not an ownership stake, and is valued as such — not by a fundamental scorecard.
_gates.evidence_needed: Rating rationale, exchange default disclosure (SEBI LODR Reg 51 / 30), 10-K subsequent events.

_gates.label: Qualified audit opinion on the financial statements
_gates.why: A qualification is the auditor formally disagreeing with a number you are about to score. The disputed item is usually exactly the one driving the flattering ratio.
_gates.evidence_needed: Basis for Qualified Opinion paragraph; quantify the effect if the auditor did.

_gates.label: Auditor resigned mid-term or was replaced without a clean stated reason
_gates.why: Auditors rarely walk away from fee income. A mid-term exit is the single highest-information governance signal available, and it usually precedes restatement.
_gates.evidence_needed: India: resignation letter filed under SEBI LODR + NFRA/ICAI context. US: Item 4.01 8-K and the Item 304 disagreement disclosure.

_gates.label: Material restatement of prior-period financials
_gates.why: A restatement invalidates the multi-year series that every trend, CAGR and own-history comparison in this scorecard rests on.
_gates.evidence_needed: Restated comparatives in the annual report; US Item 4.02 8-K (non-reliance).

_gates.label: Cumulative operating cash flow below 50% of cumulative reported profit over 3+ years
_gates.why: Sustained divergence between profit and cash is the most reliable quantitative precursor of accounting failure. Over one year it is working capital; over three or more it is a claim that has never been collected in cash. Averaging a great ROCE against it hides the exact thing that makes the ROCE untrustworthy.
_gates.evidence_needed: Five-year cash flow statements: sum CFO, sum PAT, show the ratio. State the explanation offered and whether it is credible.

_gates.label: [India] More than 50% of promoter holding pledged
_gates.why: Heavy pledging couples the share price to control. A price fall triggers margin calls, invoked shares and forced selling — a reflexive spiral that is independent of business quality and has repeatedly destroyed otherwise sound companies.
_gates.evidence_needed: Quarterly shareholding pattern, Table on encumbered shares; trend over 8 quarters.

_gates.label: [India] 25-50% of promoter holding pledged, or pledging rising
_gates.why: Same mechanism, earlier stage. The direction of travel matters more than the level.
_gates.evidence_needed: Shareholding pattern trend; stated purpose of the pledge.

_gates.label: Material unexplained related-party transactions or promoter-group fund diversion
_gates.why: Value can be perfectly real and still never reach minority shareholders. Related-party leakage is a claim on cash flows that never appears in any ratio in this scorecard.
_gates.evidence_needed: Related-party note (Ind-AS 24 / ASC 850), audit committee approvals, loans and advances to group entities, corporate guarantees.

_gates.label: Unconsolidated subsidiaries, opaque group structure, or material unaudited components
_gates.why: What is not consolidated cannot be scored. Historically, the entity that fails is the one that was never in the reporting perimeter.
_gates.evidence_needed: Subsidiary list, 'Other Matters' paragraph on unaudited components, JV/associate accounting basis.

_gates.label: Receivables or unbilled revenue growing far faster than sales for 2+ years
_gates.why: Revenue that has not been collected is a hypothesis. Sustained divergence usually resolves as a write-off, not a collection.
_gates.evidence_needed: Receivable days and unbilled revenue over 5 years vs revenue growth; ageing schedule; expected credit loss provisioning trend.

_gates.label: [India] Exchange surveillance action (ASM / GSM / trade-for-trade) or SEBI restraint order
_gates.why: Surveillance placement changes the tradability, margin requirement and price-discovery quality of the security regardless of the fundamentals.

_gates.label: Repeated equity issuance at or below book value without a clear returns case
_gates.why: Per-share value is what the owner receives. A company that funds growth by continuously selling cheap equity can grow every headline number while making each share worth less.
_gates.evidence_needed: Share count over 5-10 years, issue prices vs book, use of proceeds.

_gates.label: Board or audit committee independence materially compromised
_gates.why: Every governance control in this scorecard assumes someone independent is checking. If nobody is, the other governance metrics measure disclosure, not conduct.
_gates.evidence_needed: Board composition, independent-director resignations and their stated reasons, audit committee membership and attendance.

_gates.label: Analyst cannot explain the revenue model or the key accounting judgement
_gates.why: A confident composite on a business you cannot explain is a false signal that reads exactly like a real one. Capping it forces the report to say so.
_gates.evidence_needed: State plainly what could not be understood and what would resolve it.

generic.label: Generic (non-financial operating company)
generic.notes: Fallback metric set. Applies to any operating company where EBIT, invested capital and free cash flow are meaningful. It is NOT valid for banks, NBFCs, insurers or REITs — those have their own standalone sets because the standard ratios there are undefined or inverted.

moat_width_score.label: Moat width and direction

anchors.2: No identifiable advantage; price-taker
anchors.5: Local or contractual advantage, stable
anchors.8: Structural advantage (scale, network, switching costs) demonstrably widening

moat_width_score.note: Justify with evidence: market share trend, pricing vs input costs, customer retention, returns persistence.

anchors.2: Cannot pass through input costs
anchors.5: Passes through with a 1-2 quarter lag
anchors.8: Prices ahead of costs; gross margin stable or rising through an input spike

roce_pct.label: ROCE (%)
roce_pct.note: EBIT / (net debt + equity + capitalised leases). Compare to the company's own cost of capital, not to another sector.

roic_wacc_spread_pp.label: ROIC - WACC spread (pp)
roic_wacc_spread_pp.note: The single most sector-portable profitability measure, because WACC already absorbs local rates and business risk.

opm_pct.label: Operating margin (%)
opm_pct.note: Deliberately low-weighted. Margin level is a function of value-chain position, not quality — see the sector overrides.

gross_margin_pct.label: Gross margin (%)
gross_margin_pct.note: Read the trend, not the level. Definitions differ across filers; check what sits above the line.

roe_pct.label: ROE (%)
roe_pct.note: Always read with leverage. A high ROE on 3x debt/equity is a different fact from the same ROE debt-free.

cfo_to_pat_3y.label: Cumulative CFO / PAT, 3y (x)
cfo_to_pat_3y.note: The core cash-conversion test. Sustained readings below 0.5 trigger the cashflow_profit_divergence gate.

fcf_margin_pct.label: FCF margin (%)
fcf_margin_pct.note: CFO less full capex. If separating maintenance from growth capex, state the split and the basis.

accruals_ratio_pct.label: Accruals ratio (%)
accruals_ratio_pct.note: (NI - CFO - CFI) / average net operating assets, or the simpler (NI - CFO) / average total assets. State which.

other_income_share_of_pbt_pct.label: Other income as % of PBT
other_income_share_of_pbt_pct.note: High other income means the operating business is smaller than the headline profit suggests.

effective_tax_rate_pct.label: Effective tax rate (%)
effective_tax_rate_pct.note: India new regime ~25.2%; US federal 21% plus state. A persistently sub-normal rate needs an explanation (SEZ/holiday/loss carry-forward) with an expiry date.

net_debt_to_ebitda.label: Net debt / EBITDA (x)
net_debt_to_ebitda.note: Include capitalised leases and acceptances. Negative (net cash) clamps at 10.

current_ratio.label: Current ratio (x)
current_ratio.note: A very high current ratio is idle capital, not strength.

near_term_maturity_cover_x.label: Liquidity / next-12m debt maturities (x)
near_term_maturity_cover_x.note: (Cash + undrawn committed lines + expected FCF) over the maturity wall. Refinancing risk kills solvent companies.

cash_conversion_cycle_days.label: Cash conversion cycle (days)
cash_conversion_cycle_days.note: Heavily sector-dependent; negative is normal and good for retail, FMCG and subscription models.

revenue_cagr_5y_pct.label: Revenue CAGR, 5y (%)
revenue_cagr_5y_pct.note: Nominal. In a high-inflation market, decompose into volume, price and mix before believing it.

eps_cagr_5y_pct.label: EPS CAGR, 5y (%)
eps_cagr_5y_pct.note: Per share, always. Absolute profit growth funded by dilution is not growth for the owner.

roiic_pct.label: Return on incremental invested capital (%)
roiic_pct.note: Change in NOPAT over change in invested capital, measured over 3-5 years to damp noise. This is the metric that decides whether growth creates or destroys value.

anchors.2: Saturated; incremental capital goes to buybacks or worse acquisitions
anchors.5: Several years of visible reinvestment at current returns
anchors.8: Decade-long runway at or above current returns, evidenced by penetration data

organic_share_of_growth_pct.label: Organic share of growth (%)
organic_share_of_growth_pct.note: Serial acquirers can be excellent, but acquisition-led growth must be tested against goodwill and ROIIC, not revenue.

promoter_insider_holding_pct.label: Promoter / insider holding (%)
promoter_insider_holding_pct.note: [India] promoter holding from the quarterly shareholding pattern. [US] founder/insider beneficial ownership from DEF 14A. Skin in the game is good; near-total control with a thin float is not.

promoter_pledge_pct.label: [India] Promoter shares pledged (% of promoter holding)
promoter_pledge_pct.note: Levels above 25% also trigger a gate. Track the direction over 8 quarters.

anchors.2: Value-destroying M&A, buybacks at peaks, unrelated diversification
anchors.5: Adequate; reinvests sensibly, no disasters
anchors.8: Demonstrated countercyclical discipline; buys assets cheap, returns cash when it cannot

anchors.2: Segment data withheld, guidance missed silently, hostile concalls
anchors.5: Compliant disclosure, adequate segments
anchors.8: Discusses failures unprompted, gives unit economics, restates history when definitions change

dilution_5y_pct.label: Share count change, 5y (%)
dilution_5y_pct.note: Include SBC, convertibles, warrants and ESOP pools on a fully diluted basis.

fcf_yield_pct.label: FCF yield (%)
fcf_yield_pct.note: FCF to equity holders over market cap, or unlevered FCF over EV — state which.

pe_x.label: P/E (x)
pe_x.note: Meaningless for deep cyclicals at the peak or trough of a cycle — use mid-cycle earnings or drop the metric.

multiple_vs_own_10y_median_pct.label: Current multiple vs own 10y median (%)
multiple_vs_own_10y_median_pct.note: The cleanest sector-neutral valuation input available: the company is its own control group.

reverse_dcf_growth_gap_pp.label: Price-implied growth minus defensible growth (pp)
reverse_dcf_growth_gap_pp.note: Converts valuation from an opinion into a testable claim. State the reverse-DCF assumptions.

anchors.2: Loss-making at trough, needed rescue capital last cycle
anchors.5: Profitable but sharply lower at trough
anchors.8: Cash-generative through the last full cycle without dilution

anchors.2: Price or licence set by regulator with an adverse review pending
anchors.5: Normal regulated exposure
anchors.8: Minimal single-point regulatory dependence

input_fx_exposure_score.label: Input cost / FX exposure (10 = low risk)

anchors.2: One founder holds the customer relationships and the strategy; no succession
anchors.5: Strong second line, founder still central
anchors.8: Institutionalised; a CEO change would not alter the thesis

esg_controversy_score.label: Environmental / social / litigation exposure (10 = low risk)

banks.label: Banks and deposit-taking lenders
banks.notes: Standalone set — does NOT extend generic. For a bank, debt is raw material rather than financing, so invested capital, EV, net debt/EBITDA and ROIC are undefined or meaningless. Score ROA and ROE together with capital adequacy; a high ROE on thin CET1 is leverage, not skill. Indian bands assume Ind-AS/RBI IRAC reporting; US bands assume GAAP/CECL. GNPA and Stage 3 / NPL are not identical definitions — say which you used.

casa_ratio_pct.label: [India] CASA ratio (%)
casa_ratio_pct.note: US equivalent: non-interest-bearing demand deposits as % of deposits (poor 8 / avg 15 / good 25 / excellent 35). The deposit franchise, not the loan book, is what a durable bank multiple pays for.

anchors.2: Bulk deposits and CDs funding loan growth; deposit beta above 60%
anchors.5: Retail-led but repricing with the cycle
anchors.8: Granular retail deposits, low beta, growing faster than credit

fee_income_to_assets_pct.label: Core fee income / average assets (%)
fee_income_to_assets_pct.note: Exclude treasury gains — those are market luck, not franchise.

roa_pct.label: Return on assets (%)
roa_pct.note: The leverage-neutral profitability measure for a lender. Prefer it to ROE.

nim_pct.label: Net interest margin (%)
nim_pct.note: India large private 3.5-4.5%, PSU 2.6-3.2%, SFBs 6-9%; US 2.8-3.6%; Europe 1.2-2.0%. Edit before use. NIM rising on unsecured mix is a different quality of earnings from NIM rising on CASA.

cost_to_income_pct.label: Cost-to-income ratio (%)
cost_to_income_pct.note: A low ratio achieved by under-investing in technology or collections is borrowed, not earned.

rorwa_pct.label: Return on risk-weighted assets (%)
rorwa_pct.note: The best single measure of whether a bank is being paid for the risk it takes.

credit_cost_pct.label: Credit cost (% of average advances)
credit_cost_pct.note: Read across a full cycle. Under-provisioning inflates every profitability metric simultaneously.

slippage_ratio_pct.label: Slippage ratio (fresh NPA formation, %)
slippage_ratio_pct.note: The forward-looking asset-quality number. GNPA is history; slippage is the future.

pcr_pct.label: Provision coverage ratio (%)
pcr_pct.note: State whether it includes technical write-offs — the two definitions differ by 10-20pp.

treasury_gains_share_of_ppop_pct.label: Treasury gains as % of pre-provision profit

nnpa_pct.label: Net NPA (%)
nnpa_pct.note: Net NPA / net worth is the real solvency question — compute it and state it in the report.

car_pct.label: Capital adequacy (CRAR, %)
car_pct.note: India: RBI minimum 11.5% including CCB for commercial banks. Score the buffer over the minimum, not the level.

credit_deposit_ratio_pct.label: Credit-deposit ratio (%)
credit_deposit_ratio_pct.note: Too high means funded by wholesale money; too low means an unproductive balance sheet.

sma2_pct.label: [India] SMA-2 / Stage 2 book (%)
sma2_pct.note: The pipeline of tomorrow's NPAs. US equivalent: criticised and classified loans.

loan_growth_vs_system_x.label: Loan growth vs system credit growth (x)
loan_growth_vs_system_x.note: Deliberately a band. A lender growing at 2-3x the system is buying market share with credit standards; the losses arrive two to three years later.

book_value_cagr_5y_pct.label: Book value per share CAGR, 5y (%)
book_value_cagr_5y_pct.note: Per share, after dilution. This is what a bank shareholder actually compounds.

promoter_insider_holding_pct.label: Promoter / parent holding (%)
promoter_insider_holding_pct.note: [India] RBI licensing conditions cap promoter holding over time — check the dilution obligation and its deadline.

anchors.2: Grew fastest into the last credit blow-up
anchors.5: Average through-cycle discipline
anchors.8: Visibly shrank a segment before losses appeared; raised capital early and cheaply

anchors.2: No sectoral/segment slippage detail, restructuring poorly disclosed
anchors.5: Regulatory minimum disclosure
anchors.8: Full slippage bridge, vintage curves, segment-wise credit cost, discussed unprompted

dilution_5y_pct.label: Share count change, 5y (%)
dilution_5y_pct.note: Banks legitimately raise capital to grow. Judge issue price vs book value, not the fact of issuance.

divergence_report_score.label: [India] RBI risk-assessment divergence record (10 = none)
divergence_report_score.note: A reported divergence in NPA or provisioning is the regulator publicly disagreeing with management's numbers.

pb_x.label: Price / book (x)
pb_x.note: P/B is only interpretable against ROE. The correct question is whether the P/B is justified by sustainable ROE minus cost of equity, not whether it is low.

htm_unrealised_loss_to_cet1_pct.label: Unrealised HTM/AFS losses as % of CET1
htm_unrealised_loss_to_cet1_pct.note: The 2023 US regional-bank mechanism: solvent on reported capital, insolvent on marked capital, and deposits leave at the speed of a mobile app.

nbfc.label: NBFCs, housing finance and non-bank lenders
nbfc.notes: Standalone set. Leverage is the product, not a flaw — score it against the regulatory ceiling and the segment norm (an HFC legitimately runs 6-8x where a gold lender runs 3-4x). The binding risk is liability-side: an NBFC fails when funding stops, not when assets deteriorate. India: RBI scale-based regulation layer (base/middle/upper) changes the applicable capital and disclosure norms — state the layer.

anchors.2: Short-term wholesale funding against long-tenor assets
anchors.5: Bank lines plus NCDs, adequately matched
anchors.8: Diversified across banks, capital markets, ECB and securitisation, tenor-matched, tested through a liquidity event

borrowing_cost_vs_peer_pp.label: Cost of borrowing vs peer median (pp)
borrowing_cost_vs_peer_pp.note: For a lender, funding cost advantage IS the moat. It is the closest analogue to low-cost production.

nim_pct.label: Net interest margin (%)
nim_pct.note: Segment-dependent: an HFC at 3% and a microfinance lender at 12% can both be excellent. Edit per segment before use.

collection_efficiency_pct.label: Collection efficiency (%)
collection_efficiency_pct.note: State the definition — current-month billing vs total including arrears differ by several points and are routinely conflated.

leverage_x.label: Debt / equity (x)
leverage_x.note: Band, not lower-better: an under-levered lender is wasting the only asset it has. Compare to the segment norm and the regulatory ceiling.

capital_adequacy_pct.label: CRAR (%)
capital_adequacy_pct.note: India: RBI minimum 15% for most NBFCs. Score the buffer.

alm_cumulative_gap_1y_pct.label: Cumulative ALM gap up to 1 year (% of outflows)
alm_cumulative_gap_1y_pct.note: Negative gap (inflows exceed outflows) is good. This is the number that decides whether the company survives a funding freeze.

aum_growth_pct.label: AUM growth (%)
aum_growth_pct.note: Band by design. Above roughly 40-50% sustained, an NBFC is almost always buying growth by loosening underwriting or entering an adjacent segment it does not understand.

related_party_to_revenue_pct.label: Related-party exposure / net worth (%)
related_party_to_revenue_pct.note: Lending to the promoter group is the classic NBFC failure mode — the loan book becomes a funding line for the parent.

disclosure_quality_score.label: Disclosure quality (ECL model, stage movement, co-lending)

single_state_concentration_pct.label: Largest state / region exposure (%)
single_state_concentration_pct.note: Geographic concentration converts a local political or weather event into a solvency event — repeatedly demonstrated in Indian microfinance.

rate_sensitivity_score.label: Rate-cycle sensitivity (10 = low risk)
rate_sensitivity_score.note: Fixed-rate assets funded by floating-rate borrowings is the compression trap.

insurance.label: Life, general, health and P&C insurers
insurance.notes: Standalone set. New-business strain depresses reported profit precisely when a life insurer is writing the most profitable growth, so P/E and ROE are close to useless for life — use VNB margin, ROEV and operating variances. For general/P&C the combined ratio is the whole business: below 100 means the underwriting itself makes money, above 100 means the company is a leveraged bond fund with an expensive distribution habit. Score only the metrics that apply to the sub-sector and let coverage renormalisation handle the rest.

persistency_13m_pct.label: [Life] 13th-month persistency (%)
persistency_13m_pct.note: Persistency is the honest test of whether the product was sold or mis-sold.

bancassurance_dependence_pct.label: Largest distribution channel share (%)
bancassurance_dependence_pct.note: A bank partner that can be renegotiated or lost is a single point of failure for the whole franchise.

vnb_margin_pct.label: [Life] Value of new business margin (%)
vnb_margin_pct.note: Check the product mix behind it — protection and non-par carry high margin, ULIP low. A margin jump is usually mix, not skill.

combined_ratio_pct.label: [General/P&C] Combined ratio (%)
combined_ratio_pct.note: Above 100 the underwriting loses money and profit depends entirely on investment income. India's motor third-party pool structurally lifts this — compare within sub-segment.

operating_variance_to_ev_pct.label: [Life] Operating variance as % of opening EV
operating_variance_to_ev_pct.note: Positive variances mean the actuarial assumptions were conservative and reality beat them. Persistent negative variances mean the EV was written optimistically — the closest thing to an earnings-quality test in life insurance.

reserve_development_pct.label: [General/P&C] Prior-year reserve development (%)
reserve_development_pct.note: Negative is favourable development — reserves were adequate. Persistent adverse development means current profit is borrowed from future losses.

solvency_ratio_pct.label: Solvency ratio (%)
solvency_ratio_pct.note: India: IRDAI minimum 150%. US: RBC ratio, different scale — replace the band. A ratio drifting toward the minimum means a capital raise or a growth slowdown is coming.

anchors.2: Reaching for yield in low-rated paper or illiquid assets
anchors.5: Mostly sovereign and AAA
anchors.8: Conservative, duration-matched, no credit events through the last cycle

alm_duration_gap_years.label: Asset-liability duration gap (years)
alm_duration_gap_years.note: For long-tail guaranteed liabilities the gap is the risk, and India lacks enough long-duration paper to close it fully — say so rather than scoring it silently.

gwp_growth_vs_industry_x.label: Premium growth vs industry (x)
gwp_growth_vs_industry_x.note: Band: an insurer growing at 2x the industry is usually under-pricing risk, and the claims arrive with a lag.

anchors.2: EV published with no sensitivities or assumption detail
anchors.5: Standard sensitivities disclosed
anchors.8: Full assumption set, sensitivities, and an independent actuarial review disclosed

implied_new_business_multiple_x.label: [Life] Implied new-business multiple (x)
implied_new_business_multiple_x.note: (Market cap - EV) / VNB. Makes explicit how many years of current new business the price already pays for.

guaranteed_book_pct.label: [Life] Guaranteed / non-par book as % of liabilities
guaranteed_book_pct.note: Guarantees written at high rates become a solvency problem when rates fall, and the hedge is rarely as complete as disclosed.

realestate-reit.label: REITs, InvITs and real estate developers
realestate-reit.notes: Standalone set. For a REIT the asset IS the business and is carried at fair value, so ROIC collapses toward the cap rate by construction and earnings are meaningless after depreciation — use AFFO, LTV and the cap-rate/cost-of-debt spread. Developer metrics (pre-sales, collections, unsold inventory) are tagged [DEV] and should be scored instead of the REIT set for a developer. India: REIT/InvIT distributions are governed by SEBI regulations requiring 90% distribution of net distributable cash flow — check the NDCF definition, it is not AFFO.

occupancy_pct.label: Portfolio occupancy (%)
occupancy_pct.note: Distinguish committed from in-place occupancy; the gap is future rent, not current rent.

wale_years.label: Weighted average lease expiry (years)
wale_years.note: Long WALE is cash-flow certainty but caps mark-to-market upside in a rising rent market. Read with leasing spreads.

cap_rate_spread_over_debt_pp.label: Cap rate minus cost of debt (pp)
cap_rate_spread_over_debt_pp.note: The whole economic engine of a levered property vehicle. When this spread goes negative, leverage subtracts value and the distribution is being funded by refinancing.

yield_on_cost_pct.label: Development yield on cost (%)
yield_on_cost_pct.note: Compare to the exit cap rate. Yield on cost minus market cap rate is the development spread — the only reason to build rather than buy.

affo_to_ffo_pct.label: AFFO / FFO (%)
affo_to_ffo_pct.note: The gap is maintenance capex and leasing costs — real cash that FFO pretends does not exist.

ffo_payout_ratio_pct.label: Distribution / AFFO (%)
ffo_payout_ratio_pct.note: Above 100% the distribution is funded by debt or asset sales, which is a countdown, not a yield.

collections_to_presales_pct.label: [DEV] Collections / pre-sales (%)
collections_to_presales_pct.note: Pre-sales are bookings; collections are cash. India RERA escrow rules restrict how collected money can be used — check before treating it as free cash.

ltv_pct.label: Loan to value (%)
ltv_pct.note: India: SEBI caps REIT leverage at 49% of asset value with conditions above 25%. Score the headroom to the cap, not just the level.

same_store_noi_growth_pct.label: Same-store NOI growth (%)
same_store_noi_growth_pct.note: Strips acquisitions out. This is the only growth number that tells you whether the existing portfolio is getting better.

development_pipeline_to_gav_pct.label: Development pipeline / GAV (%)
development_pipeline_to_gav_pct.note: Band: no pipeline means no growth, a large pipeline means development and funding risk on a fixed-distribution vehicle.

external_manager_fee_to_noi_pct.label: Manager fees / NOI (%)
external_manager_fee_to_noi_pct.note: Externally managed vehicles have a structural conflict: the manager is paid on assets, so it is paid to grow whether or not growth is accretive per unit.

related_party_to_revenue_pct.label: Related-party asset purchases (% of GAV)
related_party_to_revenue_pct.note: Sponsor-to-REIT asset drop-downs need an independent valuation and a unitholder vote — check both happened.

price_to_nav_discount_pct.label: Discount to NAV (%)
price_to_nav_discount_pct.note: Positive = trading below NAV. Test the NAV first: it is a valuer's opinion of cap rates, and cap rates move with the bond yield.

distribution_yield_spread_pp.label: Distribution yield minus 10y govt bond (pp)
distribution_yield_spread_pp.note: The correct sector-neutral test — a property yield must be judged against the risk-free rate of its own market, not against another country's REITs.

it-saas.label: IT services, software, SaaS and internet platforms
it-saas.notes: Margin levels here are high by construction, so the sector bands are lifted: a 20% operating margin that would be excellent in distribution is merely average in software. What actually differentiates is retention, incremental returns and whether growth survives without ever-rising sales spend. Indian IT services and US SaaS are different businesses on the same tag — services score on attrition, revenue per employee and book-to-bill; product SaaS on NRR, Rule of 40 and CAC payback.

opm_pct.note: Lifted band. Indian IT services run 20-27%; product SaaS at scale 20-35%. A 20% margin here is average, not excellent — this is the sector-relative principle in its clearest form.

roce_pct.note: Asset-light: capital employed is small, so returns are structurally high. Judge against the sector, not against a manufacturer.

net_revenue_retention_pct.label: Net revenue retention (%)
net_revenue_retention_pct.note: The single best moat proxy in software: above 100% the installed base grows without any new customer.

revenue_per_employee_kusd.label: [IT services] Revenue per employee (USD k)
revenue_per_employee_kusd.note: The productivity metric that shows whether growth is pyramid expansion or genuine value capture.

sbc_to_revenue_pct.label: Stock-based compensation / revenue (%)
sbc_to_revenue_pct.note: SBC is cash compensation paid in shares. Non-GAAP profit that adds it back is not profit. Always score fully diluted.

book_to_bill_x.label: [IT services] Book-to-bill (x)
book_to_bill_x.note: Read TCV against duration — a large TCV over seven years is a smaller annual number than it sounds.

ai_disruption_exposure_score.label: AI / platform disruption exposure (10 = low risk)
ai_disruption_exposure_score.note: Ask specifically whether the revenue is priced per seat or per unit of work, and what happens to it if the work is automated.

pharma-healthcare.label: Pharma, biotech, CDMO, hospitals and diagnostics
pharma-healthcare.notes: Four different business models on one tag. Innovators are option portfolios valued on pipeline risk-adjusted NPV; generics are commodity manufacturers with a regulatory moat and structural price erosion; CDMOs are capacity businesses; hospitals are real-estate-plus-operations with occupancy economics. Regulatory compliance is the gating variable everywhere: a single import alert can remove more value than several years of margin improvement, which is exactly why compliance sits in risk with a heavy weight rather than being averaged in.

product_concentration_top5_pct.label: Top-5 product share of revenue (%)
product_concentration_top5_pct.note: For innovators also state the patent cliff date of the largest product — a concentrated portfolio with a near cliff is a different business in three years.

chronic_share_pct.label: [India] Chronic therapy share of domestic sales (%)
chronic_share_pct.note: Chronic prescriptions repeat; acute do not. Chronic mix is the closest thing to recurring revenue in branded generics.

hospital_occupancy_pct.label: [Hospitals] Occupancy (%)
hospital_occupancy_pct.note: Band: above roughly 85% a hospital is turning patients away and needs capex, which changes the return profile.

rd_to_sales_pct.label: R&D / sales (%)
rd_to_sales_pct.note: Band and sub-sector dependent: generics 4-9%, specialty 8-14%, innovators 15-25%. Too little means no pipeline; too much without approvals means burning owner capital.

rd_capitalisation_share_pct.label: R&D capitalised (% of R&D spend)
rd_capitalisation_share_pct.note: Ind-AS/IFRS permit capitalising development costs; US GAAP largely does not. This single policy difference can move reported margin several points between otherwise identical companies.

regulatory_compliance_score.label: Regulatory compliance record (10 = clean)

anchors.2: Import alert or OAI at a plant contributing material revenue
anchors.5: Form 483 observations resolved without escalation
anchors.8: Clean EIR/VAI record across all significant sites over 5+ years

regulatory_compliance_score.note: Weighted heavily on purpose. This is a step-function risk, not a gradual one.

litigation_exposure_score.label: Litigation exposure (opioid, price-fixing, product liability) (10 = low)

payer_pricing_risk_score.label: Payer / government pricing exposure (10 = low risk)
payer_pricing_risk_score.note: [India] NLEM/DPCO price control coverage of the portfolio. [US] IRA negotiation eligibility and PBM concentration.

fmcg-consumer.label: FMCG, consumer staples, branded consumer and QSR
fmcg-consumer.notes: The sector where brand and distribution, not manufacturing, are the assets — so the scorecard weights business quality highest and balance sheet lowest. Volume growth is the honesty test: price-led growth in an inflationary year can flatter revenue while the franchise shrinks. Working capital is typically negative and should be scored as a strength, not a liquidity concern.

roce_pct.note: Asset-light branded businesses routinely earn 40%+ ROCE. Scoring them against a generic 20% 'good' band would rate almost every company excellent and destroy all discrimination.

cash_conversion_cycle_days.note: Negative working capital is normal and desirable here — the trade funds the company.

volume_growth_pct.label: Volume growth (%)
volume_growth_pct.note: The honesty test. Revenue growth net of price and mix is the only number that shows whether more people are buying more product.

ad_spend_to_sales_pct.label: Advertising & promotion / sales (%)
ad_spend_to_sales_pct.note: Band: cutting A&P is the easiest way to buy a year of margin and lose a decade of brand. Rising A&P with flat share is also a warning.

distribution_reach_score.label: Distribution reach and direct-reach growth
distribution_reach_score.note: [India] Direct reach in lakh outlets and the stockist-to-direct shift; rural share. [US/global] retail ACV distribution and shelf position.

pe_x.note: Quality staples structurally trade rich. A 30x P/E here is not the same signal as a 30x P/E in metals — which is the entire reason valuation is scored sector-relative.

private_label_disruption_score.label: Private label / D2C disruption exposure (10 = low risk)

commodity_input_exposure_score.label: Input commodity exposure and pass-through lag (10 = low risk)

auto.label: Automobiles, auto components and tyres
auto.notes: Operating leverage dominates: margin is mostly a function of utilisation, so a margin comparison across two points in the cycle compares demand, not skill. Always separate the automotive business from a captive finance arm — consolidating a lending book into an industrial balance sheet makes net debt, ROCE and leverage meaningless. Score the powertrain transition explicitly; a strong ICE franchise with no credible electrification path is a melting asset even at excellent current returns.

opm_pct.note: OEMs 6-14%, components 10-18%, tyres 12-18%. A 9% OEM margin is average; the same number would be poor for a branded consumer company and excellent for a distributor.

roce_pct.note: Compute on automotive capital employed only, excluding the finance arm.

dealer_inventory_days.label: Channel inventory (days)
dealer_inventory_days.note: [India] Wholesale dispatches minus retail registrations (VAHAN) shows whether reported sales are demand or stuffing the channel.

warranty_provision_to_sales_pct.label: Warranty provision / sales (%)
warranty_provision_to_sales_pct.note: Compare provision created against claims paid. Under-provisioning is a quiet way to lift margin for two years.

rd_capitalisation_share_pct.label: Product development capitalised (% of spend)
rd_capitalisation_share_pct.note: A major Ind-AS/IFRS versus US GAAP divergence — European and Indian OEMs capitalise heavily, US ones expense. Adjust before comparing margins across regimes.

auto_net_debt_to_ebitda.label: Automotive net debt / EBITDA, ex-finance arm (x)

anchors.2: No credible EV platform, compliance shortfall, share loss in the growing segment
anchors.5: Announced platform, launches pending, credits purchased
anchors.8: Competitive EV contribution margin ex-credits, in-house battery or secured supply, share gains

content_per_vehicle_growth_pct.label: [Components] Content per vehicle growth (%)
content_per_vehicle_growth_pct.note: The structural growth lever that lets a component supplier outgrow a flat vehicle market.

captive_finance_quality_score.label: Captive finance arm quality (10 = low risk)
captive_finance_quality_score.note: Penetration, credit cost, residual value exposure and leverage. Score it as a lender — because it is one.

metals-mining.label: Steel, aluminium, mining and commodity producers
metals-mining.notes: The only durable advantage in an undifferentiated commodity is being cheaper to produce than the marginal producer — so cost-curve position is the moat metric and carries the heaviest weight in the sector. Spot ROCE is procyclical nonsense: highest at the top of the cycle when the stock is most dangerous, negative at the bottom when it is cheapest. Score mid-cycle returns and mid-cycle leverage, state the assumed mid-cycle price, and never score a trailing P/E for a deep cyclical.

cost_curve_position_pctile.label: Position on the global cost curve (percentile, 1 = cheapest)
cost_curve_position_pctile.note: First-quartile producers earn money at prices that shut competitors down. This is the whole moat in a commodity.

reserve_life_years.label: Reserve / resource life (years)
reserve_life_years.note: Check the classification standard (JORC/NI 43-101 vs a domestic estimate) and the price assumption behind reserve conversion.

integration_captive_input_pct.label: Captive input integration (% of requirement)
integration_captive_input_pct.note: Captive iron ore, coal or bauxite is what turns a swinging spread into a stable one.

mid_cycle_roce_pct.label: Mid-cycle ROCE (%)
mid_cycle_roce_pct.note: State the mid-cycle realisation assumed and show the sensitivity. This replaces roce_pct, which is disabled for this sector.

ebitda_per_tonne_vs_peer_pct.label: EBITDA per tonne vs peer median (%)

net_debt_to_midcycle_ebitda.label: Net debt / mid-cycle EBITDA (x)
net_debt_to_midcycle_ebitda.note: Leverage measured on peak EBITDA is how cyclical companies enter restructuring while reporting a 1.5x ratio.

capex_intensity_vs_da_x.label: Capex / depreciation (x)
capex_intensity_vs_da_x.note: Band: below 1x for years is liquidation by depreciation; far above 1x at the top of the cycle is the classic capital-destruction pattern.

ev_ebitda_x.note: On mid-cycle EBITDA. Low trailing EV/EBITDA at a cycle peak is the single most common cyclical value trap.

pe_x.note: Only meaningful on normalised earnings. A trailing P/E of 4 at the peak usually signals expensive, not cheap.

resource_nationalism_score.label: Licence, royalty and resource-nationalism exposure (10 = low risk)
resource_nationalism_score.note: [India] auction-based mine allocation, royalty and DMF levies, captive block conditions.

oil-gas.label: Oil & gas — upstream, refining, marketing and gas utilities
oil-gas.notes: Three unrelated businesses under one tag: upstream is a price-taking resource depletion business, refining is a spread business, marketing and gas distribution are regulated volume businesses. Score the segment that drives profit and say which. In India, state-owned refiners and marketers carry subsidy and price-control exposure that can override every operating metric in a given year — that belongs in risk and in the report, not buried in an average.

reserve_replacement_ratio_pct.label: [Upstream] Reserve replacement ratio (%)
reserve_replacement_ratio_pct.note: Below 100% the company is consuming itself; production growth funded by depletion is not growth.

gross_refining_margin_premium_usd_bbl.label: [Refining] GRM premium over benchmark crack (USD/bbl)
gross_refining_margin_premium_usd_bbl.note: Complexity (Nelson index) and crude flexibility are what create a durable premium; a good year for cracks is not.

subsidy_price_control_score.label: Subsidy / administered-price exposure (10 = low risk)
subsidy_price_control_score.note: [India] Under-recoveries on LPG and fuel, and the timing and certainty of government compensation.

energy_transition_score.label: Energy transition / terminal value exposure (10 = low risk)
energy_transition_score.note: For a depleting-asset business the terminal value assumption is the valuation. State the assumed reserve life against the demand outlook.

utilities-power.label: Power generation, transmission and regulated utilities
utilities-power.notes: The return here is set by a regulator, not earned competitively, so the question is not 'how high is the ROE' but 'is the allowed ROE being achieved, and is the asset base growing'. Leverage is structurally high and legitimately so — a 4x net debt/EBITDA that would be alarming for a manufacturer is normal for a regulated network with contracted cash flows, which is why the sector bands are loosened. In India, counterparty risk sits with state distribution companies and shows up as receivable days, not as a credit rating.

allowed_vs_achieved_roe_gap_pp.label: Achieved minus allowed RoE (pp)
allowed_vs_achieved_roe_gap_pp.note: [India] CERC/SERC norms fix an allowed RoE on approved equity, with incentives for availability. [US] the allowed ROE comes from the rate case. Beating it means operating outperformance; missing it means under-recovery.

ppa_tie_up_share_pct.label: Capacity tied up under long-term PPAs (%)
ppa_tie_up_share_pct.note: Merchant capacity is a commodity exposure inside what looks like a regulated business.

plant_availability_pct.label: Plant availability / PLF (%)
plant_availability_pct.note: Technology-dependent: for renewables the equivalent is CUF (solar ~20-25%, wind ~25-35%). Replace the band before scoring a renewables IPP.

discom_receivable_days.label: [India] Receivable days from discoms
discom_receivable_days.note: The characteristic Indian power-sector failure: profit is booked, cash sits with a loss-making state utility.

regulatory_assets_to_equity_pct.label: Regulatory assets / under-recoveries as % of equity
regulatory_assets_to_equity_pct.note: A regulatory asset is profit recognised now on the promise of a future tariff order. Test whether past ones were actually recovered.

net_debt_to_ebitda.note: Loosened band. Contracted, regulated cash flows support leverage that would be reckless in a cyclical business.

rab_growth_pct.label: Regulated asset base growth (%)
rab_growth_pct.note: For a regulated utility, growth in the asset base at the allowed return IS earnings growth. It is the cleanest growth metric in the sector.

infra-capitalgoods.label: Infrastructure, EPC, capital goods and defence
infra-capitalgoods.notes: Percentage-of-completion accounting makes revenue and profit an estimate rather than an observation, so earnings quality carries the heaviest weight in this sector. The characteristic failure is an order book that grows while cash does not: unbilled revenue, retention money and claims accumulate on the balance sheet, and years later become a write-off. Off-balance-sheet bank guarantees and performance bonds are real leverage and must be added to the solvency view.

order_book_to_revenue_x.label: Order book / trailing revenue (x)
order_book_to_revenue_x.note: State the execution period. A 3x book over six years is weaker than a 2x book over two.

unbilled_revenue_to_revenue_pct.label: Unbilled revenue / revenue (%)
unbilled_revenue_to_revenue_pct.note: Revenue recognised on a percentage-of-completion estimate but not yet billable. Rising unbilled revenue with flat cash is the sector's signature warning.

claims_to_networth_pct.label: Arbitration claims recognised / net worth (%)
claims_to_networth_pct.note: Claims booked as assets are litigation outcomes recognised as profit. Check the historical realisation rate before believing any of it.

fixed_price_orderbook_pct.label: Fixed-price share of order book (%)
fixed_price_orderbook_pct.note: Fixed-price contracts without input escalation clauses transfer commodity risk onto a thin-margin contractor.

client_receivable_quality_score.label: Counterparty quality of the order book (10 = low risk)
client_receivable_quality_score.note: Government and state-entity clients pay late; private capex clients cancel. Both are risks, differently shaped.

telecom-media.label: Telecom, towers, broadcasting and media
telecom-media.notes: A perpetual-capex utility with consumer-brand economics on top. The binding constraint is the balance sheet: spectrum and network capex are funded with debt, and the sector's history is of leverage, not competition, deciding survivors. Score FCF after spectrum payments, because pre-spectrum free cash flow flatters every operator. For media, the accounting judgement that matters is content amortisation policy — it sets margin almost at will.

ebitda_margin_pct.label: EBITDA margin (%)
ebitda_margin_pct.note: Post-IFRS-16/Ind-AS-116 margins are inflated by lease accounting. Compare on a consistent basis or use EBITDAaL.

roce_pct.note: Structurally low: enormous capital base. A 12% ROCE here is a good business; the same number in software would be poor.

arpu_growth_pct.label: ARPU growth (%)
arpu_growth_pct.note: In a saturated market ARPU is the only real growth lever, and it is a proxy for whether the industry has stopped competing on price.

capex_to_revenue_pct.label: Capex / revenue (%)
capex_to_revenue_pct.note: Band: too little means the network falls behind and churn follows; too much means the returns will never be earned.

net_debt_to_ebitda.note: [India] Include AGR and deferred spectrum liabilities to the government — they are debt regardless of where they sit.

anchors.2: Long straight-line amortisation of content with no impairment history
anchors.5: Standard accelerated policy
anchors.8: Fast, viewership-linked amortisation with disclosed impairments

market_position_score.label: Market structure position (subscriber and revenue share trend)

spectrum_regulatory_score.label: Spectrum, licence and regulatory exposure (10 = low risk)

aviation-hotels.label: Airlines, hotels, travel and restaurants
aviation-hotels.notes: High operating leverage against fixed capacity, which means margins swing violently and the balance sheet decides who survives the swing. Always capitalise leases: an airline or hotel operator that leases its assets is not less levered, only differently disclosed — score on EBITDAR and adjusted net debt. Liquidity measured in months of fixed costs is the metric that actually predicted which operators survived the last demand shock.

rask_cask_spread.label: [Airlines] RASK minus CASK (per ASK, local minor units)
rask_cask_spread.note: The entire airline business in one number. Report both legs — a positive spread from collapsing costs is a different fact from one from strong yields.

cask_ex_fuel_vs_peer_pct.label: [Airlines] CASK ex-fuel vs peer median (%)
cask_ex_fuel_vs_peer_pct.note: Cost leadership is the only durable moat in aviation. Fuel is common to everyone; ex-fuel cost is the company.

load_factor_pct.label: [Airlines] Passenger load factor (%)
load_factor_pct.note: Read with yield. A high load factor bought with discounting is a cost, not an achievement.

revpar_index_rgi.label: [Hotels] RevPAR index vs competitive set (RGI)
revpar_index_rgi.note: Indexed to the local competitive set, so it strips out the cycle and measures relative execution — the sector-relative principle built into a single metric.

asset_light_fee_share_pct.label: [Hotels] Managed/franchised fee income share (%)
asset_light_fee_share_pct.note: Fee income is annuity-like and needs no capital; owned rooms are a levered property bet with an operating business attached.

liquidity_months_fixed_costs.label: Liquidity in months of fixed costs
liquidity_months_fixed_costs.note: The survival metric. In a demand shock, revenue goes to near zero while fixed costs continue; everything else is secondary.

deferred_revenue_days.label: Forward bookings / deferred revenue (days of revenue)
deferred_revenue_days.note: Customer float funds the business — a genuine negative working capital advantage. It also reverses violently when demand stops.

fuel_hedge_score.label: [Airlines] Fuel and FX hedging discipline (10 = low risk)

retail-ecommerce.label: Retail chains, e-commerce, marketplaces and quick commerce
retail-ecommerce.notes: Thin margins by construction, so return on capital is driven by turnover and negative working capital, not by margin — the clearest illustration in this whole scorecard of why a low-margin retailer can be a better business than a high-margin manufacturer. Score store-level economics before consolidated margins: a chain with strong unit economics and heavy new-store investment looks worse on consolidated numbers precisely because it is doing the right thing. Ind-AS 116 / IFRS 16 shifted lease costs below EBITDA — compare pre-lease store EBITDA across companies or the comparison is meaningless.

opm_pct.note: A 5% operating margin here is average; the same number would be alarming in software. The margin band is the sector's, not the market's.

roce_pct.note: The whole point of retail: 3-5% net margin multiplied by high asset turnover and negative working capital can produce a 25%+ ROCE.

cash_conversion_cycle_days.note: Deeply negative is excellent — suppliers fund the inventory. But test whether it is genuine terms or stretched payables hiding a liquidity problem.

sssg_pct.label: Same-store sales growth (%)
sssg_pct.note: Decompose into footfall, conversion, basket size and price. Growth that is only new stores can continue until the map runs out and then stops.

store_payback_years.label: New store cash payback (years)
store_payback_years.note: The single number that decides whether store expansion creates or destroys value.

contribution_margin_pct.label: [E-commerce] Contribution margin after delivery and discounts (%)
contribution_margin_pct.note: Before corporate overhead but after every variable cost of serving the order. If this is negative at scale, scale makes it worse.

take_rate_pct.label: [Marketplace] Net revenue take rate (%)
take_rate_pct.note: Also check gross vs net revenue recognition — GMV-based reporting is not revenue.

inventory_days.label: Inventory days
inventory_days.note: Rising inventory days in retail nearly always ends in markdowns, which arrive as a margin shock one or two quarters later.

platform_disruption_score.label: Disruption exposure (quick commerce, platform shift) (10 = low risk)

chemicals-cement.label: Specialty chemicals, agrochemicals, fertilisers and cement
chemicals-cement.notes: Two economics under one tag. Cement is a regional, freight-limited commodity where the moat is a limestone lease plus a short lead distance, and EBITDA per tonne is the comparable unit. Specialty chemicals sits between commodity and pharma — the moat is customer qualification and process IP, so the test is whether margins survive a Chinese supply restart. In both, per-unit metrics compared to regional peers beat any absolute margin band.

ebitda_per_tonne_vs_peer_pct.label: [Cement] EBITDA per tonne vs regional peer median (%)
ebitda_per_tonne_vs_peer_pct.note: Regional, not national: cement prices and costs are local because freight limits the market to a few hundred kilometres.

lead_distance_km.label: [India, cement] Average lead distance (km)
lead_distance_km.note: Freight is one of the largest cost lines. Short lead distance is a structural, un-copyable cost advantage.

power_fuel_cost_vs_peer_pct.label: Power & fuel cost per tonne vs peer (%)
power_fuel_cost_vs_peer_pct.note: Captive power, WHRS and green power share drive this and are durable.

backward_integration_score.label: Backward integration and key raw material security

new_product_revenue_share_pct.label: [Chemicals] Revenue from products launched in last 5y (%)
new_product_revenue_share_pct.note: The innovation pipeline test that separates a specialty chemicals company from a commodity producer calling itself one.

china_supply_exposure_score.label: Chinese / low-cost supply restart exposure (10 = low risk)
china_supply_exposure_score.note: Many 'specialty' margins were China-shutdown windfalls. Ask what the margin was before the disruption and what happens when supply returns.

environmental_compliance_score.label: Environmental compliance and pollution-control record (10 = clean)
environmental_compliance_score.note: [India] State pollution control board closure orders can halt a plant with no notice — a step-function risk, like FDA action in pharma.

holdco-assetmgr.label: Holding companies, conglomerates, AMCs and alternative managers
holdco-assetmgr.notes: Consolidated ratios blend unrelated businesses into a number no manager can act on, so score look-through economics and value sum-of-the-parts. Governance carries the heaviest weight of any sector here because the entire question is whether value at the subsidiary level ever reaches the holdco shareholder. A wide discount to NAV is only an opportunity if there is a mechanism to close it; without one it is a permanent, rational tax on the structure.

look_through_roe_pct.label: Look-through ROE on proportionate stakes (%)
look_through_roe_pct.note: Weight each holding's ROE by the holdco's economic interest. Consolidated ROE is an artefact of which stakes cross the consolidation threshold.

opex_to_nav_pct.label: Holdco operating cost / NAV (%)
opex_to_nav_pct.note: The running cost of the structure itself. Capitalised at a market multiple, a 1% cost drag explains a large part of most holdco discounts.

dividend_upstreaming_pct.label: Dividends received / look-through profit (%)
dividend_upstreaming_pct.note: Tests whether subsidiary profit actually reaches the parent, or is permanently trapped where minorities cannot access it.

net_flows_to_opening_aum_pct.label: [AMC] Net flows / opening AUM (%)
net_flows_to_opening_aum_pct.note: Separates flows from market appreciation. Only flows are the business; market moves are borrowed.

yield_on_aum_bps.label: [AMC] Revenue yield on AUM (bps)
yield_on_aum_bps.note: [India] SEBI TER caps compress yield as AUM grows — model the slab effect rather than extrapolating current yield.

performance_fee_share_pct.label: [Alt manager] Performance fees as % of revenue
performance_fee_share_pct.note: Carry and performance fees are real but lumpy and cycle-dependent. Capitalising them at a management-fee multiple is a standard valuation error.

holdco_discount_to_nav_pct.label: Discount to sum-of-the-parts NAV (%)
holdco_discount_to_nav_pct.note: Score with the crystallisation metric below, never alone. A 60% discount that has been 60% for fifteen years is a structural fact, not an opportunity.

anchors.2: No buyback, no distribution, promoter benefits from the structure
anchors.5: Occasional dividends, discount stable for years
anchors.8: Active buybacks below NAV, announced demerger or stake monetisation with a timetable

anchors.2: Related-party asset transfers at unfavourable prices, minorities diluted in restructurings
anchors.5: Compliant, unremarkable
anchors.8: Restructurings priced independently, minorities consistently offered the same terms as the promoter

structure_complexity_score.label: Structural complexity and tax leakage (10 = simple)
structure_complexity_score.note: Each layer of cross-holding adds a discount and a tax on upstreamed dividends. Count the layers and say what each costs.

shipping-logistics.label: Shipping, tankers, dry bulk, ports and logistics
shipping-logistics.notes: Shipping is the purest supply-cycle business in the market: rates are set by the global orderbook, not by any operator's skill, so score the balance sheet and the entry price rather than current profitability. Asset value matters more than earnings — price to NAV on vessel values is the primary valuation tool and trailing P/E is actively misleading at both cycle ends. Asset-light logistics has different, better economics and should be scored on the generic set plus network density.

rate_to_cash_breakeven_x.label: Achieved rate / cash breakeven (x)
rate_to_cash_breakeven_x.note: Cash breakeven includes opex, drydocking, interest and debt amortisation. Below 1.0 the company is consuming equity every day it operates.

opex_per_day_vs_peer_pct.label: Vessel opex per day vs peer (%)

fleet_age_years.label: Average fleet age (years)
fleet_age_years.note: Read with environmental regulation: older, less efficient tonnage faces CII/EEXI restrictions and a widening earnings gap.

contracted_revenue_days_pct.label: Contracted revenue days, next 12m (%)
contracted_revenue_days_pct.note: Coverage is protection at the top of the cycle and an opportunity cost at the bottom. Judge it against where the cycle is.

net_debt_to_vessel_value_pct.label: Net debt / fleet market value (%)
net_debt_to_vessel_value_pct.note: Vessel values fall with rates, so leverage rises exactly when earnings collapse. This double effect, not the rate itself, is what bankrupts shipowners.

price_to_nav_x.label: Price / net asset value on vessel values (x)

industry_orderbook_to_fleet_pct.label: Industry orderbook / global fleet (%)
industry_orderbook_to_fleet_pct.note: The single best forward indicator of shipping returns. A low orderbook is the precondition for a rate cycle; a high one guarantees its end.

exchanges-payments.label: Exchanges, depositories, clearing houses, rating agencies and payment networks
exchanges-payments.notes: Some of the best economics in any market: network effects, negative working capital, and near-zero incremental cost per transaction, which is why the ROCE and margin bands are lifted far above the generic set. Invested capital can be negative because customer float funds the business — say so explicitly rather than reporting an absurd ROIC. The concentrated risk is regulatory: a single rule change on product mix, fee caps or market structure can remove a large share of revenue overnight, which is why risk is weighted above the default.

opm_pct.note: A 45% operating margin is merely average here. Scored on the generic band it would read as world-class — the sector-relative point in one line.

roce_pct.note: If invested capital is near zero or negative, report ROCE as not meaningful rather than as infinity, and lean on margin and cash generation instead.

take_rate_trend_bps_3y.label: Take rate change over 3 years (bps)
take_rate_trend_bps_3y.note: The most under-monitored line in the sector. Volume growth of 20% with take rate down 15% is barely growth at all — always decompose revenue into volume, price and mix.

float_income_share_of_pbt_pct.label: Float / treasury income as % of PBT
float_income_share_of_pbt_pct.note: Float income is a rate bet inside an operating business. It inflates profit in a high-rate year and vanishes in a low-rate one.

anchors.2: Majority of revenue from one product that a regulator has publicly proposed restricting
anchors.5: Normal regulated exposure across several products
anchors.8: Diversified across products, geographies and regulators

semiconductors.label: Semiconductors, fabs, equipment and capital-intensive hardware
semiconductors.notes: A cyclical industry with software-like gross margins and utility-like capex, so both the margin bands and the capital intensity bands are lifted. Judge returns across a full cycle: capacity decided three years ago meets demand today, which is why peak-cycle ROIC flatters and trough-cycle ROIC misleads. R&D and capex are not optional costs — under-spending buys two good years and then permanent process irrelevance, which is why both are scored as bands rather than lower-is-better.

cycle_adjusted_roic_pct.label: Cycle-adjusted ROIC (%)
cycle_adjusted_roic_pct.note: Average across a full cycle, stating the years used. A single-year ROIC in this industry says more about the cycle than the company.

rd_to_sales_pct.label: R&D / sales (%)
rd_to_sales_pct.note: Band: under-investing is a slow exit from the industry; over-investing without design wins is capital destruction.

capex_to_sales_pct.label: Capex / sales (%)
capex_to_sales_pct.note: Fabless companies sit at the low end legitimately; a fab operator at the low end is falling behind on node.

anchors.2: Two nodes behind with no roadmap
anchors.5: Competitive at mainstream nodes
anchors.8: At or ahead of the leading edge, or dominant in a defensible mature niche

customer_concentration_top5_pct.note: Loosened band: extreme customer concentration is structurally normal in this industry, so the generic band would misprice it.

inventory_days.label: Inventory days
inventory_days.note: Channel inventory build is the classic late-cycle signal — check distributor inventory as well as the company's own.

design_win_pipeline_score.label: Design-win pipeline and revenue visibility
design_win_pipeline_score.note: Design wins convert to revenue with a two to four year lag, so this is the only forward-looking growth evidence available.

geopolitical_exposure_score.label: Geopolitical / export-control exposure (10 = low risk)
geopolitical_exposure_score.note: Concentration of fabs, customers or export licences in a single jurisdiction is a tail risk that no operating metric captures.

mortgage-reit-specialty-finance.label: Mortgage REITs, BDCs and specialty finance vehicles
mortgage-reit-specialty-finance.notes: Standalone set -- does NOT extend generic. These are levered spread vehicles, not operating companies: there is no revenue, no EBIT, no invested capital and no cash conversion cycle, so operating margin, ROCE, EV/EBITDA and net debt/EBITDA are undefined rather than merely different. Nearly the entire balance sheet is marked to model or to market, so book value is the unit of account and ECONOMIC RETURN (change in book value per share plus dividends declared, over opening book value per share) is the only honest measure of what the owner earned -- a 14% dividend yield paid out of a 12% book value decline is a return of capital. Score an agency mREIT, a credit mREIT and a BDC on different absolute levels: agency vehicles legitimately run 6-8x leverage on 1.0-1.7% spreads, credit vehicles 2-4x on wider spreads, and BDCs are capped near 2.0x by the 150% asset coverage requirement. RANGES BELOW ARE INDICATIVE STARTING POINTS ONLY. Where you have a genuine peer set (same asset class, same leverage convention, same quarter-end marks), PEER-PERCENTILE COMPARISON OVERRIDES THESE BANDS -- pass peer_values or peer_percentile and score.py will use them in preference.

permanent_capital_share_pct.label: Term / non-mark-to-market funding as % of liabilities
permanent_capital_share_pct.note: Unsecured notes, CLO liabilities, convertibles and term facilities cannot be margin-called. Every mortgage REIT failure on record was a funding failure: the assets were fine and the repo lender re-marked them. This is the single most important structural quality metric in the sector.

funding_diversity_score.label: Funding counterparty diversity and depth

anchors.2: Three or fewer repo counterparties, no committed lines, no unsecured issuance record
anchors.5: Ten-plus counterparties, some committed capacity, one unsecured deal done
anchors.8: Twenty-plus counterparties, laddered committed facilities, repeat unsecured issuance through a stress window

funding_diversity_score.note: Count committed versus uncommitted capacity separately. Uncommitted repo disappears exactly when it is needed.

asset_selection_edge_score.label: Asset selection and underwriting edge

anchors.2: Buys the index; no origination, servicing or sourcing advantage
anchors.5: Some proprietary sourcing or a servicing affiliate
anchors.8: Proprietary origination or workout capability that demonstrably produced better realised losses than the asset class

asset_selection_edge_score.note: In a spread vehicle the only durable edges are cheaper funding and better sourcing. Everything else is beta dressed as skill.

economic_return_pct.label: Economic return (BVPS change + dividends, % of opening BVPS)
economic_return_pct.note: The headline number for the sector and the only one that cannot be gamed by paying an unearned dividend. Compare it to the vehicle's own cost of equity (commonly 10-13%), and read it over at least three years -- one good quarter of spread tightening flatters it.

net_interest_spread_pct.label: Net interest spread (asset yield minus cost of funds, %)
net_interest_spread_pct.note: State whether hedge carry (swap/SOFR receive-fixed income) is inside the spread -- including it can add 100-200bp and the two conventions are routinely compared as if identical. Band set for a hybrid agency/credit book; a direct-lending BDC runs 5-7%.

portfolio_yield_pct.label: Weighted average portfolio yield (%)
portfolio_yield_pct.note: Band, not higher-better: above the band the yield is being bought with credit risk or PIK, below it the vehicle is not earning its cost of equity. Set for a credit/BDC book -- reset to roughly [3.5, 7] for an agency MBS portfolio before scoring one.

dividend_coverage_by_core_eps_x.label: Core / distributable EPS / dividend declared (x)
dividend_coverage_by_core_eps_x.note: Band: below 1.0x the distribution is being funded from capital or leverage; far above 1.0x a REIT is failing its 90% distribution requirement or hoarding, and the excess is usually about to be paid as a special. Check what management excludes from 'distributable earnings' -- realised credit losses are commonly excluded, which is precisely the item that matters.

non_accrual_pct.label: [BDC] Non-accrual investments (% of portfolio at fair value)
non_accrual_pct.note: Quote at fair value AND at cost -- the gap is how much has already been written down. Non-accruals at cost running well above the fair-value figure means the marks moved before the accrual status did.

pik_income_share_pct.label: [BDC] PIK income as % of total investment income
pik_income_share_pct.note: Payment-in-kind income is interest the borrower could not pay in cash, accrued into the balance sheet and distributed to shareholders in cash. Rising PIK share alongside flat non-accruals is the classic sequence in which credit deterioration is deferred rather than avoided.

leverage_debt_to_equity_x.label: Leverage (debt / equity, x)
leverage_debt_to_equity_x.note: Band, not lower-better: an under-levered spread vehicle is not earning its cost of equity, and leverage is the product. Set for a hybrid/credit book. Agency-only mREITs run 6-8x legitimately (reset the band up); BDCs are capped near 2.0x by the 150% asset coverage test (reset it down and score the headroom to the ceiling, not the level).

repo_maturity_days.label: Weighted average remaining repo / secured funding maturity (days)
repo_maturity_days.note: The tenor of the funding is the tenor of the company. Thirty-day repo against thirty-year mortgages is a maturity mismatch of roughly 360x, and it is renewed on the lender's terms every month. Report the maturity ladder, not just the average.

unencumbered_assets_to_equity_pct.label: Unencumbered assets + cash as % of equity
unencumbered_assets_to_equity_pct.note: This is the margin-call absorption capacity. It answers the only question that matters in a stress week: how far can spreads widen before the vehicle is a forced seller?

debt_maturity_within_12m_pct.label: Debt maturing within 12 months (% of total debt)
debt_maturity_within_12m_pct.note: Include repo rolls only if they are uncommitted. For BDCs this is the unsecured note wall -- refinancing an unsecured maturity while trading below book usually means issuing equity at a discount to do it.

book_value_change_1y_pct.label: Book value per share change, 1y (%)
book_value_change_1y_pct.note: For a levered spread vehicle, book value per share is the whole growth story -- there is nothing else compounding. Persistent erosion alongside a maintained dividend means the distribution is a partial liquidation. Always read this together with economic_return_pct rather than instead of it.

net_portfolio_growth_pct.label: Net portfolio / investment growth (%)
net_portfolio_growth_pct.note: Band: rapid portfolio growth in a spread business is almost always funded by issuing equity or by moving down in credit, and shrinkage is often the correct decision when spreads are tight. Neither direction is good on its own.

external_manager_fee_to_equity_pct.label: Management + incentive fees as % of average equity
external_manager_fee_to_equity_pct.note: Externally managed vehicles have the sector's defining conflict: the manager is paid on equity or assets, so it is paid to raise and deploy capital whether or not doing so is accretive per share. Check whether the incentive fee has a total-return hurdle with a high-water mark, or is charged on net investment income alone -- the latter pays the manager for taking credit risk that has not yet been realised as a loss.

equity_issuance_premium_to_book_pct.label: Weighted average equity issuance price vs book value (%)
equity_issuance_premium_to_book_pct.note: Positive = issued above book, accretive to existing holders. Issuing below book transfers value from existing shareholders to the manager's fee base and is the most common way these vehicles destroy per-share value while growing every headline number. Look at the ATM programme, not just marketed deals.

insider_ownership_pct.label: Manager / insider ownership (%)
insider_ownership_pct.note: Some alignment matters a great deal in an externally managed structure. Near-total insider control of a listed spread vehicle is a different problem -- minority holders cannot force internalisation or a wind-down.

valuation_marks_independence_score.label: Independence of fair-value marks

anchors.2: Manager marks Level 3 positions with no third-party review
anchors.5: Rotating third-party review covering part of the book annually
anchors.8: Independent valuation firm reviews effectively the whole Level 3 book every quarter, with the board's valuation committee documenting disagreements

valuation_marks_independence_score.note: In a BDC nearly the entire portfolio is Level 3, so 'book value' is an opinion produced by the party paid on it. Who forms that opinion is a first-order fact, not a disclosure detail.

anchors.2: No repo maturity ladder, no vintage or LTV detail, hedge notional disclosed without tenor
anchors.5: Regulatory minimum schedules
anchors.8: Full funding ladder by counterparty, hedge notional by tenor, portfolio stratified by vintage/LTV/FICO or by loan-to-value and EBITDA, and rate/spread sensitivities published every quarter

price_to_book.label: Price / book value (x)
price_to_book.note: The primary valuation anchor because the balance sheet is already at fair value. But a discount to book is not automatically cheap -- it usually means the market disbelieves the marks, disbelieves the dividend, or is charging for the external management fee. Test which before treating it as a margin of safety.

dividend_yield_spread_over_10y_pp.label: Dividend yield minus 10y government bond (pp)
dividend_yield_spread_over_10y_pp.note: The sector-neutral way to read a double-digit yield: against the risk-free rate of its own market and its own date. A 13% yield with the 10y at 4% is a different proposition from the same yield with the 10y at 1%. Score it only if dividend_coverage_by_core_eps_x is at or above 1.0x.

price_to_core_eps_x.label: Price / core (distributable) EPS (x)
price_to_core_eps_x.note: Secondary to price_to_book. Core EPS is a management-defined non-GAAP measure in this sector -- state the exclusions before using the multiple.

hedge_ratio_pct.label: Hedge notional as % of repo / funding liabilities
hedge_ratio_pct.note: Band: under-hedging leaves book value exposed to a rate move, and over-hedging past 100% converts the vehicle into a directional rate bet in the other direction. The notional alone is not the answer -- state the hedge tenor against the asset duration, since a fully hedged notional at the wrong point on the curve is not a hedge.

cpr_prepayment_pct.label: Constant prepayment rate (CPR, % annualised)
cpr_prepayment_pct.note: Band, and the direction inverts with the price of the book: for a portfolio held at a premium to par, fast prepayment destroys the premium; for a discount book it pulls the discount forward and is favourable. State the portfolio's average dollar price, then reset this band accordingly. Extension risk (CPR collapsing far below the band) is the mirror danger and is what lengthens duration precisely when rates rise.

interest_rate_sensitivity_bvps_pct.label: Modelled BVPS change for a +100bp parallel shift (absolute %)
interest_rate_sensitivity_bvps_pct.note: Enter the absolute magnitude of the modelled move, whichever direction is worse. This is the company's own duration-gap disclosure, so also state whether it includes spread widening -- most published shocks are rate-only, and every crisis in the sector was a spread event, not a rate event.

top10_issuer_concentration_pct.label: Top-10 borrower / issuer exposure (% of portfolio)
top10_issuer_concentration_pct.note: Meaningful for credit mREITs and BDCs; near-irrelevant for an agency book, where the sole credit exposure is the GSE guarantee. Drop the metric rather than scoring it for an agency vehicle.

insurance-brokers-services.label: Insurance brokers, underwriting agencies and insurance services
insurance-brokers-services.notes: Distribution and advice, not underwriting -- brokers take no balance-sheet risk on claims, which is what separates this set from the 'insurance' key and makes the generic operating metrics valid here. The economics are among the best in financial services: recurring commissions on renewing policies, negative working capital from fiduciary float, and a fragmented acquisition pond that has funded three decades of roll-ups. That last point is where the analysis has to be sharpest -- almost every headline growth number in the sector is partly bought, so ORGANIC growth and the goodwill it sits on are the two numbers that decide whether the roll-up is compounding or laundering. Leverage bands are loosened because contracted, recurring, low-capex cash flow supports more debt than a manufacturer's. RANGES BELOW ARE INDICATIVE STARTING POINTS ONLY; where a comparable peer set exists (same commission accounting, same fiduciary-interest treatment, aligned fiscal periods), PEER-PERCENTILE COMPARISON OVERRIDES THESE BANDS -- pass peer_values or peer_percentile.

opm_pct.note: GAAP operating margin, which sits several points below the adjusted EBITDAC margin the sector reports. Score both and state the bridge -- amortisation of acquired customer relationships is the item that separates them, and it is a real cost of the acquisitions that produced the growth.

roce_pct.note: Depressed by construction: a serial acquirer's capital employed is mostly goodwill from deals done at 10-15x EBITDA. Returns on TANGIBLE capital are near-infinite and equally uninformative. Judge the roll-up on ROIIC against acquisition multiples paid, not on this.

net_debt_to_ebitda.note: Loosened band. Recurring renewal commissions with near-zero maintenance capex support more leverage than a cyclical operating business, and the large brokers run 3-4x routinely. Exclude fiduciary cash and fiduciary liabilities from both sides -- that money belongs to insurers and insureds, not to the broker, and consolidating it distorts every leverage ratio in the sector.

ev_ebitda_x.note: Lifted band: quality brokers structurally trade at 15-22x EBITDA on the strength of retention and organic growth. Use EBITDAC consistently on both sides of the ratio.

pe_x.note: Lifted band. Recurring renewal commissions on a fee-based, near-capex-free business earn a structurally high multiple, and the large brokers have traded at 22-30x for most of the last decade. Strip fiduciary investment income out of earnings before applying it, or a rate cycle will look like a de-rating.

organic_revenue_growth_pct.label: Organic revenue growth (%)
organic_revenue_growth_pct.note: The single most important number in the sector, and the one most often defined loosely.
